title: M&A Comps and Transaction Multiples
description: Master how to select, analyze, and adjust precedent transactions to value acquisition targets.

interactions.prompt: Why do precedent transaction multiples typically exceed trading multiples for comparable public companies?

options.text: Acquirers pay a control premium for ownership rights
Public markets always undervalue companies
Transaction data is reported with a time lag
Investment banks inflate deal prices for higher fees

interactions.teachingPreamble: Precedent transaction analysis values a company by examining prices paid in comparable M&A deals. When Microsoft acquired Activision Blizzard for $68.7B in 2022, it paid roughly 30% above Activision's pre-deal trading price. This premium over market price - called a control premium - reflects the value of owning and directing the entire business.

interactions.prompt: Three recent SaaS acquisitions show EV/Revenue multiples: Deal A (2021 bull market) 18x, Deal B (2023 downturn) 8x, Deal C (2023 downturn) 9x. What's the most critical adjustment before using these as comps?

options.text: Average all three for the most reliable estimate
Use only Deal A since it's the highest value
Adjust for market conditions - Deal A reflects a different cycle
Discard all deals older than six months

interactions.prompt: An acquirer expects $200M in annual cost synergies from a deal. The target's standalone EV/EBITDA is 10x. What does the synergy-adjusted multiple roughly become if the target has $800M EBITDA?

options.text: 8x, because synergies reduce the effective price paid
12x, because synergies increase the target's value
10x, synergies don't affect the transaction multiple
15x, synergies are always added to the purchase price

interactions.teachingPreamble: Synergies - cost savings or revenue gains from combining two businesses - are a key driver of M&A premiums. When Kraft merged with Heinz in 2015, the deal thesis centered on $1.5B in cost synergies. Analysts separate the 'price paid for the standalone business' from the 'price paid for synergies' to understand if acquirers overpaid - EV of $8B ÷ ($800M EBITDA + $200M synergies) = 8x.

interactions.prompt: In precedent transactions, the ____ premium measures the percentage above the target's unaffected share price that the acquirer pays to gain full ownership.

options.text: Liquidity
Control
Synergy
Minority

interactions.prompt: You're valuing a mid-cap healthcare target. You have 3 highly comparable deals from 2019 and 8 loosely comparable deals from the last 12 months. Which set do you anchor your analysis on?

options.text: The 3 highly comparable deals despite being older
The 8 recent deals to capture current market conditions
Use recent deals as primary, older deals as a check
Discard both and rely solely on DCF

interactions.prompt: A target was acquired for $5B EV with LTM EBITDA of $400M and NTM EBITDA of $500M. Which multiple pairing best reveals whether the acquirer paid for growth?

options.text: Compare LTM 12.5x vs NTM 10.0x - the gap signals growth value
Only use NTM 10.0x since forward metrics are more accurate
Only use LTM 12.5x since it reflects actual performance
Average them to get 11.25x for the best estimate

interactions.teachingPreamble: Transaction multiples can be calculated on last-twelve-months (LTM) or next-twelve-months (NTM) financials. When Salesforce acquired Slack for $27.7B, the LTM revenue multiple was ~26x but the NTM multiple was ~20x, reflecting Slack's rapid growth. Comparing LTM and NTM multiples side by side reveals how much of the purchase price is attributable to expected growth versus current performance.

interactions.prompt: Rank these factors from MOST to LEAST important when selecting comparable precedent transactions for a U.S. specialty chemicals acquisition: (a) Deal size, (b) Industry sub-sector match, (c) Geographic market, (d) Transaction date recency.

options.text: Deal size similarity
Industry sub-sector match
Geographic market overlap
Transaction date recency

interactions.prompt: Your precedent transaction set showed a median EV/EBITDA of 11x. News breaks that two of your five comp deals involved distressed sellers accepting below-market offers. How should you adjust?

options.text: Remove distressed deals; median likely rises to 12-13x
Keep all five deals for the largest possible sample
Flag distressed deals but show both adjusted and unadjusted ranges
Replace them with public trading comps instead

interactions.priorContext: You previously built a precedent transaction analysis with five comparable deals showing a clean median of 11x EV/EBITDA. Now you learn that two sellers were under financial distress, meaning those transaction prices may not reflect fair market value and could be dragging your median down.
